errors: No computational errors; the page contains plans and remarks, not derivations.
The function field is written as 'y^λ + x^λ + 1' with '= 0' implicit. With z = −1 this corresponds to x^λ + y^λ = z^λ for odd λ.

The regularity programme is only sketched. The uniform-approximation plus integration-by-parts route does not by itself give higher derivatives without additional hypotheses, e.g. regularity F_{y'y'} ≠ 0. That condition is not stated here.

results.what: Programme to prove that a minimizing function of ∫F(x,y,y')dx has higher derivatives, via rational approximation and integration by parts (Euler–Lagrange expression vanishing)
results.modern_name: Regularity of extremals (du Bois-Reymond lemma / Hilbert's differentiability theorem); precursor of Hilbert's 19th problem
results.usually_credited_to: du Bois-Reymond (1879); Hilbert (differentiability theorem, c.1899–1900, cf. Bolza); 19th problem solved by Bernstein 1904, De Giorgi/Nash 1957

results.what: Attack Fermat's Last Theorem by studying the function field of x^λ + y^λ + 1 = 0 arithmetically (prime ideals, à la Kronecker)
results.modern_name: Arithmetic of the Fermat curve / function-field methods
results.usually_credited_to: Kronecker, Dedekind–Weber (1882) for arithmetic of function fields; Fermat-curve arithmetic geometry 20th century

deep.surprise_reason: These are early research notes (late 1880s notebook): plans, not results. The regularity programme matches Hilbert's known later work and the 19th/20th problems. The Fermat-curve function-field idea is an interesting but undeveloped suggestion in the Kronecker spirit. The existence-statement remark is a known flavour of Hilbert's thinking. Notable as documentation of early interests, not as new mathematics.
